title: Simplified Processing Procedures / New-Construction Condominium and ADU Condominium Projects / Ordinance
motion: I THEREFORE MOVE, that the Department of City Planning, with the assistance of the Department of Building and Safety, and the Bureau of Engineering, within 30 days, to draft an ordinance to utilize the City's authority under State law to establish simplified and expedited processing procedures for eligible new-construction condominium and ADU 1 Stanford Center on Longevity, Home Ownership Analysis, Stanford Sightlines Project, Stanford Univ. See: https://longevity.stanford.edu/home-ownership-2/. 2 Research by the Local Initiatives Support Corporation (LISC) shows that small-lot town homes are 42 percent cheaper t'han adjacent single-family homes, and subdividing lots into separately owned units can expand the City's property tax base by $500 million to $7.5 billion over 20 years. 3 Assembly Bills 1903 and 7406 ~ SEP 1 6 2026 . ... condominium projects. The ordinance should identify and address all streamlining possibilities including but not limited to: • An administrative procedure for waiving parcel, tentative, and final map requirements including a streamlined process for making the statutory findings required by California Government Code Section 66428(b), including but not limited to requirements as to site area, design, floodwater drainage control, publ ic road access, sanitary sewage disposal, water supply availability, and environmental protection; • Opportunities to eliminate duplicative review requirements currently imposed through the City's condominium and subdivision review processes such as bu ilding permits, zoning review, utility review, or other permitting processes, while maintaining applicable health, safety, infrastructure, and other substantive requirements; and • Streamlined coordination of subdivision, condominium-plan, building-permit, and Certificate of Occupancy processes.
